cohort: The study included 200 pregnant women from a tertiary care hospital, categorized into obese (BMI >= 30 kg/m2, n=100) and non-obese (BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2, n=100) groups.
finding: Maternal obesity was significantly associated with higher rates of various maternal complications (GDM, gestational hypertension, pre-eclampsia, cesarean delivery, induction of labor, intraoperative complications, PPH) and adverse fetal/neonatal outcomes (macrosomia, preterm birth, shoulder dystocia, neonatal hypoglycemia, low Apgar scores, and NICU admissions).
mod_finding: Obese women had significantly higher rates of cesarean delivery (52% vs 29%) and induction of labor (42% vs 21%).
